title_guess: National income: the four GDP variants and why product, income and expenditure totals are equal

segments.teaches: GDP comes in four variants (real or nominal, at factor cost or market price); India's headline figure is nominal GDP at market price, and the video asks why

elements.what: heading with a big red numeral 4 and a blue underline: ways of calculating GDP
the four variant labels typed one under another, bold first word
maroon India silhouette beside the list
pink band behind the nominal-at-market-price line (the one India reports)
orange Hindi 'why?' word next to the highlighted line

segments.notes: List lines appear about 0.8 s apart. The Hindi 'why?' tag opens the question the rest of the video answers.
segments.idea: GDP has four variants; India reports nominal GDP at market price, and the video asks why
segments.shown_as: four variant lines type on under a heading with a big red 4; an India silhouette sits beside the list; a pink band lights the nominal-at-market-price line and a 'why?' tag pops next to it

segments.teaches: real GDP needs a base year; countries use different base years and India's is FY2012

elements.what: national flags as column heads: Pakistan, USA, India, China
one-row cream strip under the flags with a BASE YEAR row label; dashes in other columns, India's cell filled with FY 2012
BASE YEAR chip at the left end of the strip
blue box drawn around the 'real GDP' word
short vertical connector from the boxed real GDP up to the base-year chip

segments.notes: Flags are used as quick column headers; only one cell gets a value, so the eye goes straight to India.
segments.idea: real GDP needs a base year; countries use different ones and India's is FY 2012
segments.shown_as: four national flags become column heads over a one-row BASE YEAR strip; only India's cell fills (FY 2012); a box drawn round 'real GDP' is joined up to the base-year chip
segments.example: India's base year FY 2012; other countries left blank

segments.teaches: national income family: GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP; we start from GDP

elements.what: cream NATIONAL INCOME heading chip, top left
four abbreviation rows each joined by a short red dash to its full form
green band on the GDP row
green tick after GDP

segments.notes: Abbreviation + dash + expansion is a recurring list style in this channel.
segments.idea: national income has four measures (GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP); we start with GDP
segments.shown_as: four abbreviations, each joined by a short red dash to its full form, under a NATIONAL INCOME chip; a green band and a tick pick out GDP

segments.teaches: national income is about the total of products; begin with one person's income as a building block

elements.what: the word 'Product' inside the GDP expansion boxed in dark green
dotted curved arrow from the NATIONAL INCOME chip down to the boxed word, with a small '?'
black arrow from the GDP row to a sigma sign
big sigma followed by 'Products'
single blue person icon
cream panel MY INCOME with a red 2000 Rs value, joined to the person by a thin line

segments.notes: The other three aggregate rows vanish and GDP slides up. Start of a running numeric example (2000 Rs).
segments.idea: national income is a total of products; build it up starting from one person's income
segments.shown_as: the other rows vanish and GDP slides up; 'Product' is boxed and an arrow leads to a big sigma 'Products'; one person icon appears, tied by a thin line to a MY INCOME panel reading 2000 Rs

segments.teaches: adding everyone's income in a family gives family income

elements.what: five blue person icons standing together inside a pink panel
lines fanning down from the family to each member's income: 1000, 100, 4000, 5000 Rs plus the earlier 2000
MY FAMILY'S INCOME caption with the red total 12100 Rs

segments.notes: Running example: one income 2000 grows to a family sum of 12100. Person icon multiplies into the family.
segments.idea: add every member's income and you get the family's income
segments.shown_as: the person icon multiplies into a family of five in a pink panel; lines fan from the family to each income (2000, 1000, 100, 4000, 5000) and a red total 12100 Rs appears

segments.teaches: national income is the sum of incomes of everyone living within India's geographical boundary

elements.what: India silhouette at the left end of a wide cream band
long row of identical teal person icons filling the band (about 30)
definition line under a black rule, with a green tick chip in front
green tick on the definition

segments.notes: Scale-up trick across three segments: one person, then a family, then the whole country as a crowd row.
segments.idea: national income is the total income of everyone living inside India's borders
segments.shown_as: the family is swapped for a long band of about 30 identical person icons running out from an India silhouette; a ticked definition line is written under it

segments.teaches: sum of incomes equals sum of products equals national income; sum of expenditure is added as the third equal

elements.what: sigma Income = sigma Products = NATIONAL INCOME (chip); then sigma Expenditure prepended
cream NATIONAL INCOME chip at the end of the equation

segments.notes: Equation grows from the left; this three-way identity stays at the top for the rest of the video.
segments.idea: total income = total product = total spending = national income
segments.shown_as: an equation grows from the left: sigma Income = sigma Products = NATIONAL INCOME chip, then sigma Expenditure slides in at the front

segments.teaches: a product is made by four factors of production, and each factor earns an income: profit, rent, wages and salaries, interest

elements.what: grey panel 'Factors of Production' listing entrepreneur, land, labour, capital
blue arrows from each factor into a framed product picture
laptop inside a light-blue frame as the product
blue band on the left listing the factor incomes profit, rent, wages and salaries, interest, appearing one by one
values 4K, 2K, 2K, 2K written to the left of each factor income

segments.notes: The equation slides to the top to make room. Running numeric example continues: factor incomes total 10K.
segments.idea: a product is made by four factors of production, and each factor earns an income: profit, rent, wages, interest
segments.shown_as: the equation slides to the top; a panel lists entrepreneur, land, labour, capital and blue arrows run from each into a framed laptop; the matching incomes appear one by one on a blue band with values 4K, 2K, 2K, 2K

segments.teaches: the same 10,000 appears three ways: incomes paid to factors, value of the product, and what the buyer spends, so all three totals match

elements.what: blue customer figure on the right
'Paid' arrow from customer to product and 'Sold' arrow from product to customer
small price bubble above the customer: 10,000 Rs
sum line under the factor incomes: 10K = 10,000 rupees; 10,000 rupees under the product frame
10,000 rupee labels popping above each sigma term of the top equation
cream boxes lighting up behind sigma Expenditure, sigma Products and sigma Income in turn

segments.notes: One laptop priced 10,000 proves the three methods agree. Equation terms get value labels one at a time with a glow.
segments.idea: the same 10,000 is the factors' income, the product's value and the buyer's spending, so the three totals match
segments.shown_as: a customer appears; a 'Paid' arrow goes to the laptop and a 'Sold' arrow comes back, with a 10,000 Rs price bubble; 10,000 labels pop over sigma Income, Products and Expenditure in turn as each term glows
segments.example: one laptop sold for 10,000 Rs = factor incomes 10K = buyer's spending 10,000

elements.what: split card: next-video panel with a loading bar and a grey playlist panel

segments.shown_as: next-video panel with a loading bar beside a grey playlist panel

recurring_cast: person (grows into a family, then a crowd row)
running_examples: one income 2000 Rs -> family 12100 Rs -> everyone in India

best_moments.why: one person icon multiplies into a family and the incomes are summed: 'add everyone up' is seen, not told
a long row of people running out from the India map makes 'everyone inside the border' obvious
one laptop's 10,000 shown as the factors' income, the product's value and the buyer's payment proves the three methods agree

weak_moments.why: opening is a typed list of four variants with a map badge; text only
abbreviation list with dashes; text only
